build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: it was called the poor man's Ferrari, but the thing it was actually mocked for was the engine. The California T was the first turbocharged Ferrari road car since the F40 went out of production, and purists treated the twin-turbo V8 as Ferrari giving up the naturally aspirated scream to sell a cheaper car. 552 hp and roughly 557 lb-ft, in the model nobody took seriously.
2. Cover where Ferrari went next, because it changes what this car is. The mid-engine car is now a plug-in hybrid V6 - the 296 GTB, 819 hp, the first six-cylinder road car to wear the Ferrari badge, since the old Dino never did - and Ferrari has revealed its first electric car, the Luce. So the engine this car was punished for is the one people now want, and this is the cheap way into that V8.
3. For the head-to-head use the naturally aspirated Ferrari California it replaced - 4.3-litre V8, 453 hp, no turbos, the same folding hardtop 2+2 shape. The turbo car it was looked down on for is nearly 100 hp up on it.

script: The return of turbo technology marks the evolution in road cars. Since the legendary F40, no Ferrari had embraced forced induction until the 2015 California T. Ferrari California T’s distinct yellow brake calipers house carbon ceramic brakes, showcasing its racing DNA. Twin-turbocharged V8 engines produce 553 hp and 557 lb-ft of torque, delivering thrilling performance with each acceleration. It hits zero to sixty in 3.6 seconds. The Ferrari California T’s engine was criticized for straying from tradition, yet now it's hailed as a perfect blend of innovation and performance. Racetrack-inspired carbon fiber steering wheels highlight the fusion of performance and luxury inside the California T. Its engine is a 3.9L twin-turbo V8. Originally costing around $200,000, California Ts now sell for about $100,000, reflecting significant depreciation over the years. With Ferrari embracing turbo power and hybrid technology, does the California T offer the best of both worlds?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2015 Ferrari California T, finished in Rosso Corsa with a black interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 17,000 miles. This California T is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes 20-inch wheels, carbon ceramic brakes, Scuderia Ferrari fender shields, a power-folding hardtop, leather upholstery, power-adjustable Daytona-style front seats, and carbon fiber interior trim. The seller reports no notable modifications. Service documentation in the gallery indicates that this California T had the transmission replaced in December 2025, at 14,215 miles. Designed by Pininfarina, the California made its debut for the 2009 model year as Ferrari's entry-level model. It was envisioned as a daily-drivable roadster, so it offered four seats and amenities not often associated with past models, such as a conventional navigation system. It was also Ferrari's first standard production model to feature a dual-clutch transmission, a power-folding hardtop, and a front-engine V8 configuration. The California T was introduced for the 2015 model year and featured a turbocharged power plant – the first in a Ferrari since the legendary F40. Power comes from a 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8, rated at 553 horsepower and 557 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
